report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of correctness.py: digest, freeze_selection, _check_selection, BeforeState, judge_before_state, CorrectnessResult, judge_after_state, _run_lists.
risks: line 841-854 | high | digest property imports hashlib locally and is only defined on Selection; if any caller invokes digest on a non-Selection object, AttributeError; but within this chunk it's only used on Selection instances. | Check all call sites of .digest to confirm they are Selection objects.

line 898-910 | medium | freeze_selection deliberately does not validate node ids; a task with a non-string node id (e.g., int) would be accepted and later cause type errors in runner. | Confirm task schemas always provide strings for fail_to_pass/pass_to_pass/test_overlay.

line 905 | medium | test_revision is taken as-is from task.get('test_revision'); if missing, it becomes None, and downstream code may not handle None. | Verify that a missing test_revision is handled elsewhere (e.g., resolve_revision).

line 925-951 | medium | _check_selection compares observed vs declared node sets but does not check for duplicate node ids within the observed dicts; a runner could report the same node twice with different statuses and the check would pass. | Confirm that runners deduplicate node ids before returning statuses.

line 1011-1017 | medium | judge_before_state uses NO_VERDICT, PROVEN_NOT_PASSING, STATUS_PASSED, STATUS_MISSING constants that are not defined in this chunk; if any of these are misspelled or not imported, runtime NameError. | Verify these constants exist and are imported in the module.
line 1011-1017 | medium | judge_before_state assumes f2p and p2p dicts have string keys; if a node id is not a string, sorted() may raise TypeError. | Confirm node ids are always strings.

line 1044-1058 | medium | CorrectnessResult.ok returns True only for OUTCOME_FIXED, but the docstring says 'including could_not_run' — the docstring is correct but the property does not explicitly handle other outcomes; it's fine because it returns False for any non-fixed. | No action needed; just noting.

line 1066-1083 | medium | judge_after_state computes regressed by checking after_p2p against before.p2p; if before.p2p is empty (e.g., no PASS_TO_PASS declared), then any non-passing after_p2p node is not regressed (since before.p2p.get(n) is None), which is correct. | Confirm that before.p2p always contains only declared nodes.

line 1089-1110 | medium | _run_lists calls runner(worktree, list(selection.fail_to_pass), ...) and runner(worktree, list(selection.pass_to_pass), ...); if selection.fail_to_pass is empty, runner may still be invoked with an empty list, which could cause an error. | Confirm TestRunner handles empty node lists.

line 1093-1095 | medium | _run_lists appends f2p_run.to_dict() to runs, but if runner raises an exception, the run is not recorded, and the exception propagates; this may be intended but could leave partial runs. | Confirm that callers handle exceptions from _run_lists.

handoff.purpose: Defines Selection.digest, freeze_selection, _check_selection guard, BeforeState dataclass, judge_before_state, CorrectnessResult dataclass, judge_after_state, and _run_lists.

symbols.name: digest
symbols.note: Property on Selection (defined elsewhere) that returns a 16-char SHA-256 hex digest of a JSON-serialized representation of the selection fields, sorted keys and compact separators.

symbols.name: freeze_selection
symbols.note: Creates an immutable Selection from a task dict, base_revision, and timeout. Deduplicates and sorts node lists; does not expand or filter; sets gate to 'pytest'.

symbols.name: _check_selection
symbols.note: Guard function that compares observed node sets (f2p, p2p) against the frozen selection's declared node sets. Returns an error string if there are extra or missing nodes, otherwise None.

symbols.name: BeforeState
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing the before-state: whether verified, base_revision, f2p/p2p statuses, reasons, invalid/unrunnable flags, duration, and the frozen selection.

symbols.name: BeforeState.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes BeforeState to a dict, including sorted f2p/p2p, reasons, flags, duration rounded to 3 decimals, and selection dict/digest if present.

symbols.name: judge_before_state
symbols.note: Pure function that takes base_revision, f2p/p2p statuses, duration, and selection, and returns a BeforeState verdict. Applies three refusal rules: unrunnable on no verdict, invalid on bad f2p, invalid on bad p2p.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing one evaluation result: task_id, outcome, reason, base_revision, change, selection, before, after statuses, fixed/unfixed/regressed nodes, duration, and runs.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult.ok
symbols.note: Returns True only if outcome == OUTCOME_FIXED; False for all other outcomes including could_not_run.

symbols.name: CorrectnessResult.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes CorrectnessResult to a dict, including nested selection/before dicts, sorted after statuses, node tuples as lists, rounded duration, and runs as list.

symbols.name: judge_after_state
symbols.note: Pure function that determines outcome after the change: could_not_run if any unknown status, regressed if any p2p that passed before now fails, not_fixed if any f2p not passing, else fixed. Returns (outcome, reason, fixed, unfixed, regressed).

symbols.name: _run_lists
symbols.note: Runs FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as two separate invocations using the frozen selection. Appends run dicts to the runs list. Returns (f2p_statuses, p2p_statuses).

claims.text: digest: returns a 16-character hex digest of the selection's content.
claims.why: The property constructs a JSON body with sort_keys and compact separators, hashes it with SHA-256, and returns the first 16 hex characters.

claims.text: freeze_selection: Node ids are taken EXACTLY as declared -- deduplicated and ordered for determinism, never expanded, never filtered, and never read from the filesystem.
claims.why: The function uses dict.fromkeys to deduplicate, sorted to order, and directly reads from task.get('fail_to_pass') etc. without any expansion or filesystem access.

claims.text: freeze_selection: There is deliberately no pattern, glob or directory walk here.
claims.why: The function only processes lists from the task dict; no glob, pattern, or directory walk appears in the code.

claims.text: freeze_selection: this function is the only place a set is ever built for an evaluation.
claims.why: This chunk does not cover the entire module; other functions like _check_selection build sets (declared/observed), but those are not 'built for an evaluation' in the same sense. The claim may refer to node sets specifically; cannot fully verify from this chunk.

claims.text: _check_selection: GUARD: the run reported on EXACTLY the frozen nodes, or say what moved.
claims.why: The function computes declared and observed sets and returns an error message listing extra or missing nodes, thus enforcing exact reporting.

claims.text: BeforeState docstring: ``verified`` is True only when every FAIL_TO_PASS node was PROVEN not to pass and every PASS_TO_PASS node passed.
claims.why: judge_before_state returns BeforeState(True, ...) only when no unknown, no bad_f2p, and no bad_p2p are found, which means all f2p are PROVEN_NOT_PASSING and all p2p are STATUS_PASSED.
The function checks for any status in NO_VERDICT and returns a BeforeState with unrunnable=True.

claims.text: judge_before_state docstring: 2. A claimed FAIL_TO_PASS node that PASSED, was SKIPPED, or is MISSING -> ``invalid``.
claims.why: bad_f2p is computed as nodes not in PROVEN_NOT_PASSING; for each, it adds a reason and eventually returns invalid=True.

claims.text: judge_before_state docstring: 3. A claimed PASS_TO_PASS node that did not pass -> ``invalid``.
claims.why: bad_p2p is computed as nodes where status != STATUS_PASSED; reasons are added and invalid=True is returned.

claims.text: CorrectnessResult.ok docstring: True only for ``fixed``. Nothing else is a pass, including ``could_not_run`` -- especially ``could_not_run``.
claims.why: The property returns self.outcome == OUTCOME_FIXED, which is True only for fixed; all other outcomes including could_not_run yield False.

claims.text: judge_after_state docstring: PRECEDENCE: could_not_run > regressed > not_fixed > fixed.
claims.why: The function checks unknown first (could_not_run), then regressed, then unfixed, and only then returns fixed.

claims.text: judge_after_state docstring: ``regressed`` next, because a change that breaks the regression set is reported as breaking it EVEN IF it also turned every FAIL_TO_PASS green.
claims.why: The regressed check is performed before the unfixed check; if any p2p that passed before now fails, it returns OUTCOME_REGRESSED regardless of f2p statuses.

claims.text: _run_lists docstring: Takes the frozen :class:`Selection`, NOT the task dict, and that is the structural half of the immutability rule.
claims.why: The function signature takes selection: Selection and uses selection.fail_to_pass and selection.pass_to_pass; it never references the task dict.

claims.text: _run_lists docstring: Two invocations on purpose: a collection error in one list must not turn the other list into ``not_run``.
claims.why: The function runs f2p_run and p2p_run separately; if one invocation fails (e.g., collection error), the other may still have been run, though the exception would propagate. The claim about 'not_run' is about the statuses of the other list being unaffected, which is true because they are separate runner calls.

observations.what: digest property imports hashlib locally; if called on a non-Selection instance, AttributeError.
freeze_selection does not validate that node ids are strings; non-string ids would pass through.
test_revision is taken as-is from task.get('test_revision'); if missing, it becomes None.
_check_selection does not check for duplicate node ids within observed sets; a runner could report the same node twice with different statuses.
judge_before_state relies on constants NO_VERDICT, PROVEN_NOT_PASSING, STATUS_PASSED, STATUS_MISSING that are not defined in this chunk.
judge_before_state assumes f2p and p2p dicts have string keys; sorted() on non-strings would raise TypeError.
CorrectnessResult.ok docstring says 'including could_not_run' but the property does not explicitly handle that case; it returns False for any non-fixed, which is correct.

judge_after_state computes regressed using before.p2p.get(n) == STATUS_PASSED; if before.p2p is empty (no PASS_TO_PASS declared), then any non-passing after_p2p node is not regressed, which is correct.
_run_lists invokes runner even if selection.fail_to_pass is empty; runner may not handle empty list.
_run_lists appends f2p_run.to_dict() to runs, but if runner raises, the run is not recorded and exception propagates.
